field.help: Internal: used only by company employees, free, multi-GPU. Public: shared with NETTRADES marketplace, earns tokens.

field.name: container_runtime
field.help: gVisor is recommended for all pools – it provides syscall-level isolation without memory hoarding. Docker is for trusted internal pools only.

field.name: scheduled_share
field.help: When checked, this node follows the company's public sharing schedule.

div.p: gVisor (recommended): Works on any Linux host, including WSL2. No KVM required. Memory returns to the host immediately when freed. GPU support via nvproxy. Install: download runsc binary from https://gvisor.dev.
Docker (fallback): Standard containers. Only for trusted internal pools behind the company firewall.
Pool change behaviour: Changing from Internal to Public automatically reconfigures WireGuard to hub-and-spoke mode (/32). Changing back to Internal restores full mesh connectivity.
macOS Detected: Public GPU sharing is not available on this machine. Apple Silicon GPUs cannot be isolated with gVisor or Kata Containers. This node can only be assigned to Pool A (Internal).

field.name: tee_capabilities
field.help: Hardware-backed security features detected on this node. Consumer GPUs will show all False – this is normal.

div.p: Nodes that support NVIDIA CC, Intel SGX, or AMD SEV-SNP can run the most sensitive workloads with hardware-guaranteed isolation. Consumer GPUs (RTX 4090, etc.) do not have these features – this is expected.
Routing sensitive workloads: When you configure inference policies, you may prefer to route high-sensitivity requests to nodes with hardware-backed Confidential Computing.

field.name: edge_device_info
field.help: Auto-detected edge device capabilities (Jetson, Raspberry Pi, Coral TPU). These fields are populated automatically by the agent.

div.p: What this means: Edge devices like NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi and Google Coral TPU can run quantized AI models on-device. If this node is an edge device, the platform can automatically deploy the appropriate model size and quantization.
Enable edge support globally: Go to GPU Manager → Multi-Modal & Edge Settings and enable “Edge Device Support”. Then select the default quantization level.

field.name: reputation_score
field.help: 100 = perfect. Drops if attestation fails or the node misbehaves.

p.b: To get this node fully operational, ensure:

ul.li: The NETTRADES GPU Agent is installed and running on the node.
WireGuard is active (public key and assigned IP are visible in the “Network” tab).
GPUStack worker is registered (GPUStack Worker ID is not empty).
Container runtime is set to gVisor (recommended) or Docker (trusted internal only).
If you see TEE capabilities all False, that is normal for consumer hardware.
If the node is an edge device, enable “Edge Device Support” in Multi-Modal & Edge Settings.
